世界史主線

九上社會・歷史｜從普世宗教到近代歐洲

羅馬帝國垮掉後，地中海「三分天下」；1453 年鄂圖曼滅掉拜占庭，一邊把古典學問推進義大利（文藝復興），一邊逼歐洲人繞過中間商去亞洲（大航海），歐洲從此走向全世界。

先讀懂一個故事

① 宗教先出場

印度：阿利安人帶來婆羅門教和種姓制度。西元前 6 世紀，釋迦牟尼反對種姓、主張眾生平等，創立佛教；西元前 3 世紀阿育王大力推廣，佛教傳到東亞、東南亞。

西亞：1 世紀耶穌在羅馬帝國統治的巴勒斯坦傳教，基督教起初被迫害；4 世紀初君士坦丁承認合法，4 世紀末狄奧多西定為國教。

② 羅馬垮掉，地中海三分天下

476 年西羅馬亡於日耳曼人，西歐進入中世紀：政治混亂，靠教會維持秩序、保存古書（羅馬公教）。

東邊的拜占庭帝國（東羅馬）政教合一，皇帝也管宗教，首都君士坦丁堡（希臘正教）。1054 年基督教分裂成羅馬公教和希臘正教。

7 世紀穆罕默德在阿拉伯半島創伊斯蘭教；8 世紀阿拉伯帝國橫跨歐亞非，巴格達最繁榮。阿拉伯人翻譯希臘羅馬典籍，也把中國的造紙術、指南針往西傳。

11 世紀塞爾柱帝國崛起，11 世紀末教宗號召十字軍東征；之後鄂圖曼崛起，1453 年滅拜占庭。

③ 1453 之後，兩件大事同時發生

文藝復興（14～16 世紀，義大利）：城市靠東西貿易致富，富商贊助藝術；拜占庭學者帶古書逃到義大利；造紙加上活字印刷讓知識流通。重心從「神」轉向「人」（人文主義）。

大航海時代（15～17 世紀）：歐洲人想要亞洲的香料、絲綢，但商路被中間商控制、價格太高；有了羅盤、更好的船和王室支持，葡萄牙向東繞非洲（狄亞士到好望角、達伽馬到印度），西班牙向西橫越大西洋（哥倫布到美洲、麥哲倫船隊環球）。歐洲的重心從地中海移到大西洋。

④ 歐洲走向全世界

美洲：西班牙滅阿茲提克、印加；天花等傳染病讓原住民大量死亡，於是從非洲運入黑奴。美洲白銀流向歐洲和亞洲，玉米、番薯傳到亞歐。

亞洲：荷蘭東印度公司以巴達維亞（今雅加達）為總部，1624 年占臺灣南部；印度先有信伊斯蘭教的蒙兀兒帝國，後被英國東印度公司蠶食，19 世紀中成為英國殖民地。

澳洲：1788 年英國建立殖民地，原住民的土地被奪走。

三條線把它串起來

  • 舞台移動：地中海（羅馬）→ 三分天下（西歐・拜占庭・伊斯蘭）→ 大西洋（新航路）
  • 古典學問接力：希臘羅馬的書由三個保管人接力：西歐教士抄書、拜占庭保存、阿拉伯翻譯 → 最後在義大利匯合
  • 東西貿易：香料、絲綢從東方來，中間商賺很多 → 義大利致富（文藝復興）、葡西想繞路（大航海）

轉捩點只有一個：1453 年鄂圖曼滅拜占庭。三條線都在這裡轉彎。

每件大事問一個「為什麼」

先自己想，再點開看答案。

為什麼中世紀西歐的教會這麼重要？

西羅馬滅亡後政治混亂，教會撐起秩序，也保存了古書。

為什麼伊斯蘭世界和文藝復興有關？

阿拉伯人翻譯了希臘羅馬典籍，又把造紙術傳到歐洲。

為什麼歐洲人要找新航路？

東方商品被中間商控制、太貴；加上航海技術進步、王室支持，也想傳播基督教。

為什麼美洲原住民大量死亡？

武力征服，加上天花等歐洲帶來的傳染病。

為什麼要從非洲運黑奴到美洲？

原住民大量死亡，莊園和礦場缺人做工。

接上學過的中國史、臺灣史

  • 長安 vs 巴格達：8 世紀同時存在的兩大國際都市：唐朝和阿拉伯帝國。
  • 造紙術的旅行：中國發明 → 阿拉伯人傳播 → 歐洲印書，文藝復興用得上。
  • 鄭和 vs 達伽馬：鄭和 1405 年起下西洋，比達伽馬 1498 年到印度早了快一百年，但明朝後來不再遠航。
  • 臺灣被捲進世界史：1624 年荷蘭占臺灣南部、1626 年西班牙占臺灣北部，都是大航海時代搶航路據點的一部分。

🎧 聽故事：8 集英文故事

每集約 2 分鐘多，從印度王子一路講到荷蘭人來到臺灣。先讀「這集在講什麼」再按播放；第一遍只抓大意，第二遍打開英文稿跟著聽，第三遍試著用中文把故事說給家人聽。

第 1 集王子走出宮殿：佛教的誕生

這集在講什麼：印度的阿利安人建立種姓制度，人一出生身分就固定；釋迦牟尼王子看見生老病死，主張眾生平等、創立佛教；阿育王在大戰後懊悔，派僧侶把佛教傳到東南亞和東亞。

先認得這幾個字：caste system（種姓制度）、enlightenment（悟道）、the Buddha（釋迦牟尼）、Ashoka（阿育王）

📄 English Script（跟著聽）

Imagine that the moment you were born, your whole life was already decided. Your job, the person you could marry, and your place in society were all fixed, and you could never change them. More than three thousand years ago in India, many people lived exactly like this.

Around 1500 BC, a people called the Aryans moved into India. There were not many of them, but they ruled over a much larger local population. So they built a religion called Brahmanism and a caste system with four levels. Priests were at the top. Next came nobles and warriors, then ordinary farmers and traders, and servants at the bottom. Your caste came from your parents, it passed to your children, and people from different castes could not marry each other.

In the sixth century BC, a young prince named Siddhartha walked out of his palace. For the first time, he saw an old man, a sick man, and a dead body. He realized that kings and servants alike cannot escape old age, sickness, and death. So he gave up his throne and spent years searching for answers. At last, sitting under a tree, he found enlightenment. People called him the Buddha. He taught that all living beings are equal, and that anyone can break free from the cycle of suffering. That idea struck right at the heart of the caste system, and many people at the bottom were drawn to it.

At first, Buddhism stayed in northern India. About two hundred years later, a king named Ashoka helped it travel. Ashoka had expanded his kingdom through war, but after one terrible battle, the bloodshed filled him with regret. He turned to Buddhism, carved its teachings on stone pillars across his land, and sent monks to other countries. That is how Buddhism reached Southeast Asia and East Asia, including China. Strangely, Buddhism later faded in India itself, where Hinduism is the largest religion today. It survived because it had already spread abroad.

So remember: the Buddha founded Buddhism, and King Ashoka spread it.

Here is a question for you. If someone told you that your future was already decided, would you accept it? Or would you walk out of the palace and look for your own answer?

📄 中文故事稿

想像一下，你出生的那一刻，人生就被決定了。你長大做什麼工作、可以跟誰結婚、一輩子站在社會的哪一層，全都寫好了，而且永遠改不了。三千多年前的印度，很多人就是這樣過一生。

大約西元前一千五百年，一群叫做阿利安人的民族進入印度。他們人數不多，卻要統治人數更多的原住民。怎麼辦呢？他們發展出婆羅門教，也建立了種姓制度，把人分成四個階級。最高的是負責祭祀的婆羅門，接著是貴族和武士剎帝利，再來是平民吠舍，最底層是首陀羅。有個口訣幫你記：婆剎吠首。身分一出生就決定，父母是什麼，孩子就是什麼，不同階級也不能通婚。

到了西元前六世紀，一位叫悉達多的王子，有一天走出宮殿，第一次看見老人、病人，還有死去的人。他突然明白，不管是國王還是奴隸，誰都逃不過生老病死。於是他放下王位，出家修行，好幾年後在一棵樹下悟道，人們尊稱他釋迦牟尼。他告訴大家：眾生平等，每個人都可以靠修行，脫離痛苦的輪迴。這句話，正好打在種姓制度的心臟上。難怪很多被壓在底層的人，一聽就被吸引。

不過，佛教一開始只在印度北方流傳。真正讓它走向世界的，是兩百多年後的阿育王。阿育王原本靠打仗擴張國土，可是在一場死傷慘重的大戰之後，他深深後悔。從此他大力推廣佛教，在各地立起石柱、刻上教誨，還派僧侶到國外傳法。佛教就這樣傳到東南亞和東亞，後來也傳進了中國。有趣的是，佛教後來在印度本地反而衰微，今天印度信仰人數最多的是印度教。它能留下來，正是因為早就傳到了國外。

所以請記住四個字：釋創阿推。釋迦牟尼創立佛教，阿育王推廣佛教，兩個人別搞混。

最後留一個問題給你。如果有人告訴你，你的未來早就注定了，你會乖乖接受，還是像那位王子一樣，走出宮殿，自己去找答案？

第 2 集被追捕的信仰：基督教從地下到國教

這集在講什麼：基督教在羅馬帝國被迫害，卻越傳越廣；君士坦丁讓它合法、狄奧多西定為國教；四七六年西羅馬亡，西歐進入中世紀，教會成為生活中心，修士抄書保存古代知識。

先認得這幾個字：legal（合法）、official state religion（國教）、the Middle Ages（中世紀）、monastery（修道院）

📄 English Script（跟著聽）

When this faith first appeared, its followers could be arrested or even killed. Yet about three hundred years later, it became the official religion of the whole Roman Empire. How did that happen?

Our story begins in Palestine in the first century, when the land was ruled by Rome. A young man named Jesus traveled from place to place, teaching that God loves every person, rich or poor. His life and words were later written down and became part of the Bible, and his followers were called Christians. By the way, the calendar we use today counts its years from the time Jesus was born.

But the Roman emperors did not like the Christians. Romans worshiped many gods, and they were also expected to honor statues of the emperor. Christians believed in only one God, so they refused to do either. Because of this, they were often punished. Strangely, the harder Rome pushed, the more people joined. Christianity said that everyone is equal and that there is hope after death. For the poor and for slaves, that was a light in the darkness.

The turning point came in the fourth century. Early in that century, Emperor Constantine made Christianity legal, so believers no longer had to hide. Near the end of the century, Emperor Theodosius made it the official state religion. Remember the difference: legal is not the same as official. Tests love to ask about it.

Then something huge happened. In 476, the Western Roman Empire fell to Germanic peoples. Western Europe slid into chaos, with kings rising and falling. In those hard times, it was the Church that held society together. From baptism to marriage to funerals, the Church was part of every step of life. In quiet monasteries, monks copied old books by candlelight, line by line, keeping ancient knowledge alive. This long period in Western Europe, starting in 476 and lasting about a thousand years, is called the Middle Ages.

But the Roman Empire did not disappear completely. Its eastern half survived for almost a thousand more years. That is the star of our next episode.

Think about this: why do some ideas spread even further when people try to stop them?

📄 中文故事稿

有一個信仰，剛出現的時候，信它的人可能被抓走，甚至丟了性命。可是過了三百多年，它卻變成整個羅馬帝國的國教。它是怎麼辦到的？

故事從一世紀的巴勒斯坦開始，那時這裡歸羅馬帝國統治。一位叫耶穌的年輕人四處傳教，說上帝愛每一個人，不分貧富貴賤。他的言行後來被記錄下來，成為《聖經》的一部分，相信他的人叫做基督徒。順帶一提，我們今天用的西元紀年，就是從耶穌出生的那一年開始算的。

可是羅馬皇帝不喜歡基督徒。羅馬人拜很多神，還要拜皇帝的雕像；基督徒只信一個上帝，兩樣都不肯拜，於是常常被迫害。奇怪的是，越是迫害，信的人反而越多。為什麼？因為基督教說人人平等、死後還有希望，這對窮人和奴隸來說，是黑暗裡的一盞燈。

轉捩點出現在四世紀。四世紀初，君士坦丁皇帝承認基督教合法，信徒不必再躲躲藏藏；到了四世紀末，狄奧多西皇帝乾脆把它定為國教。口訣是：君合狄國。合法和國教是兩件不同的事，考試最愛問你分不分得清楚。

接著，大事發生了。四七六年，西羅馬帝國被日耳曼人滅亡。西歐一下子陷入混亂，國王一個換一個，打來打去。這時候，真正撐住社會的反而是教會。一個人從出生受洗、長大結婚，到最後的喪禮，都由教會主持。修道院裡的修士點著蠟燭，一筆一筆抄寫古書，把古代的知識保存下來。西歐從四七六年開始的這一千年，就叫做中世紀，教會是這個時代的生活中心。

不過，羅馬帝國並沒有全部消失。東邊還有一半，撐了將近一千年，那就是下一集的主角。

想一想：一個被打壓的想法，為什麼有時候反而傳得更遠、更久？

第 3 集兩個羅馬：拜占庭與基督教的分裂

這集在講什麼：東羅馬撐了近千年，就是拜占庭帝國，首都君士坦丁堡位在歐亞交界；拜占庭政教合一、西歐政教分離；一零五四年基督教分裂成羅馬公教與希臘正教；拜占庭保存的古希臘書，日後傳到義大利。

先認得這幾個字：Byzantine Empire（拜占庭帝國）、Constantinople（君士坦丁堡）、the Pope（教宗）、Catholic／Orthodox（公教／正教）

📄 English Script（跟著聽）

In the last episode, the Western Roman Empire fell in 476. But did you know that the Roman Empire had an eastern half, and that it did not fall? It lasted almost a thousand more years. We call this Eastern Roman Empire the Byzantine Empire.

Its capital was Constantinople, built beside the narrow strait where Europe meets Asia. Think of it as a city standing at the door between two continents. Spices and silk from the East had to pass through it on their way west, and merchants from the West had to pass through it on their way east. So the city was rich and busy, protected by tall, thick walls. It was one of the greatest cities in the world. Its most famous building was the Hagia Sophia, a church with a giant dome that seemed to float in the air.

Both the Byzantines and the people of Western Europe were Christians, but they took different paths. In the Byzantine Empire, the emperor held the most power. He ruled the government, and he also controlled the Church. In Byzantine art, the emperor often wears a purple robe with a halo around his head, while bishops stand beside him.

Western Europe was different. After Rome fell, the kings there were weak, but the Church was strong. The Pope in Rome led the Church, and kings ruled their lands. Church and state were separate, but they often argued. For hundreds of years, popes and kings fought over who had the final say.

The two sides drifted further apart. In 1054, they finally split. The Pope in Rome and the church leader in Constantinople cut each other off. From then on, Christianity had two branches: the Roman Catholic Church, centered in Rome, and the Eastern Orthodox Church, centered in Constantinople. Be careful: this was a split in the Church, not the empire breaking into east and west.

The Byzantines did one more important thing that people often forget. They kept many ancient Greek books safe. These books sat quietly in the city for centuries. On the day the city fell, they would travel with fleeing scholars to Italy and help start a movement that changed Europe. That story comes in Episodes Five and Six.

Think about this: how can the same faith grow into such different shapes in two different places?

📄 中文故事稿

上一集我們說，西羅馬在四七六年滅亡了。可是你知道嗎？羅馬帝國還有東邊的一半，它不但沒有倒，還繼續撐了將近一千年。這個東羅馬帝國，後來被稱為拜占庭帝國。

拜占庭的首都叫君士坦丁堡，蓋在歐洲和亞洲交界的海峽旁邊。你可以把它想成一座站在兩個大陸門口的城市：東方的香料、絲綢要往西運，西方的商人要往東走，都得經過這裡。所以它又富有、又熱鬧，城牆又高又厚，是當時世界上最了不起的城市之一。城裡最有名的建築是聖索菲亞大教堂，巨大的圓頂像是從天上垂下來的一樣。

拜占庭和西歐雖然都信基督教，卻走上了兩條不同的路。在拜占庭，皇帝的權力最大，國家的事他管，宗教的事他也管，這叫做政教合一。在拜占庭的畫裡，皇帝常常穿著紫色長袍，頭上還有一圈光環，主教就站在他的身旁。

西歐就不一樣了。西羅馬滅亡之後，國王的力量很弱，教會的力量卻很強。宗教的事由羅馬的教宗負責，國家的事由國王負責，這叫做政教分離。不過分開管也常常吵架，教宗和國王為了誰說了算，爭了好幾百年。

兩邊越走越遠，終於在一零五四年正式決裂。羅馬的教宗和君士坦丁堡的大主教，互相把對方開除教籍。從此，基督教分成兩支：以羅馬為中心的羅馬公教，也就是今天的天主教；以及以君士坦丁堡為中心的希臘正教，也就是今天的東正教。注意，這是基督教的分裂，不是羅馬帝國分成東西兩半，兩件事別搞混。

拜占庭還有一個很重要、卻常被忽略的功勞：它保存了大量古希臘的書。這些書在城裡安安靜靜地躺了好幾百年，等到這座城陷落的那一天，它們會跟著學者逃到義大利，點燃一場改變歐洲的運動。那是第五集和第六集的故事。

想一想：同一個信仰，為什麼在兩個地方會長出完全不同的樣子？

第 4 集沙漠裡的知識接力：伊斯蘭與阿拉伯帝國

這集在講什麼：七世紀穆罕默德創伊斯蘭教；八世紀阿拉伯帝國橫跨三洲，只占到歐洲的伊比利半島；巴格達和長安是同時代的國際大城；阿拉伯人翻譯古典書籍、把造紙術和指南針往西傳，是知識接力的中間棒。

先認得這幾個字：Muslims（穆斯林）、the Quran（古蘭經）、Ramadan（齋戒月）、Iberian Peninsula（伊比利半島）、translate（翻譯）

📄 English Script（跟著聽）

In the seventh century, on the hot Arabian Peninsula, a merchant named Muhammad founded a new religion called Islam. It was the last of the three great world religions to appear, and it shared some ideas with Judaism and Christianity. Its followers are called Muslims. They believe in one God, called Allah, and their holy book is the Quran. Muslims pray five times a day facing their holy city. For one month each year, called Ramadan, they do not eat or drink during the daytime. And once in their life, they try to travel to the holy city on a pilgrimage. Mosques have no statues or pictures of God, because Muslims believe God cannot be drawn.

After Muhammad died, Islam spread very quickly. By the eighth century, the Arab Empire stretched across three continents: Asia, Africa, and Europe. It tried to conquer the Byzantine Empire, but it could not break the walls of Constantinople. In Europe, it only took the Iberian Peninsula in the far west, where Spain and Portugal are today. That is why, even now, you can visit churches in Spain that were once mosques.

The greatest city of the Arab Empire was Baghdad. At the same time, in the East, Tang China had Chang'an. One in the west, one in the east, both were busy international cities, with markets full of traders, silk, spices, and jewels.

But the most amazing thing about the Arabs was not their armies. It was their role as a bridge for knowledge. They translated huge numbers of ancient Greek and Roman books into Arabic, including books on math, astronomy, and medicine. They also carried Chinese inventions, paper making and the compass, toward the west. Picture a relay race. The ancient Greeks wrote down knowledge. Arab translators caught it, kept it safe, and later handed it to the Europeans. Without that runner in the middle, the Renaissance might have come many years later.

So remember the three worlds around the Mediterranean: Western Europe, Catholic, centered in Rome; the Byzantine Empire, Orthodox, centered in Constantinople; and the Islamic world, centered in Baghdad.

Think about this: a translator does not invent anything new, so how can a translator still change the world?

📄 中文故事稿

七世紀，在炎熱的阿拉伯半島，一位叫穆罕默德的商人，創立了一個新的宗教，叫做伊斯蘭教。它是三大普世宗教裡最晚出現的一個，吸收了猶太教和基督教的一些教義。信徒叫做穆斯林，他們信仰唯一的真神阿拉，經典是《古蘭經》。穆斯林每天要朝著聖城的方向禮拜五次，每年有一個月白天不吃不喝，叫做齋戒月，一生之中還要盡量去聖城朝聖一次。清真寺裡沒有任何神像，因為他們認為真神不能被畫出來。

穆罕默德過世後，伊斯蘭的勢力快速擴張。到了八世紀，阿拉伯帝國已經橫跨亞洲、非洲和歐洲三大洲。它曾經想打下拜占庭，卻攻不破君士坦丁堡的城牆，最後只在歐洲的西邊，占領了伊比利半島，也就是今天的西班牙和葡萄牙。所以今天去西班牙旅行，還能看到由清真寺改建的教堂。

阿拉伯帝國最繁榮的城市是巴格達。同一個時代，東方的唐朝有長安。一西一東，兩座國際大城，市場裡擠滿了各地的商人，堆著絲綢、香料和珠寶。

不過，阿拉伯人最了不起的地方，不是打仗，而是當知識的中間人。他們把大量古希臘、羅馬的書翻譯成阿拉伯文，數學、天文、醫學通通有。他們還把中國發明的造紙術和指南針，一路往西傳。你可以想像一場接力賽：古希臘人寫下知識，阿拉伯翻譯者接住它、保存它，再把它交給後來的歐洲人。少了這一棒，後來的文藝復興可能會晚很多年才發生。

所以，請記住三分天下：西歐是羅馬公教，中心在羅馬；拜占庭是希臘正教，中心在君士坦丁堡；伊斯蘭世界的中心，是巴格達。

想一想：一個翻譯者，雖然沒有發明新東西，為什麼也能改變世界？

第 5 集一四五三，城破之日：中世紀的落幕

這集在講什麼：塞爾柱占領耶路撒冷，教宗號召十字軍；十字軍打仗成效有限，卻讓東西貿易熱絡、義大利致富；一四五三年鄂圖曼用大砲攻破君士坦丁堡，學者帶書逃往義大利，商路被控制逼出大航海。

先認得這幾個字：the Crusades（十字軍）、Ottoman Empire（鄂圖曼帝國）、cannons（大砲）、Istanbul（伊斯坦堡）、the modern age（近代）

📄 English Script（跟著聽）

If you can remember only one year from this whole period, make it 1453. In that year, a city that had stood for a thousand years finally fell. And its fall opened two doors to a new age at the same time.

But first, let's go back to the eleventh century. A new power rose in the Islamic world, the Seljuk Empire. The Seljuks took Jerusalem, the holy city of the Christians, and they also threatened the Byzantine Empire. The Byzantines asked Western Europe for help. At the end of the eleventh century, the Pope called on Christians to form armies, march east, and take back the holy city. The soldiers sewed crosses onto their clothes, so they were called Crusaders.

The Crusades went on, on and off, for almost two hundred years, and in the end they did not achieve much as wars. But they had a surprising result. Thousands of Europeans saw the rich cities of the East with their own eyes. They brought home spices, silk, and new ideas. Trade between East and West grew busier, and the cities of Italy grew richer and richer. Keep that money in mind. It becomes very important in the next episode.

Next came the Ottoman Empire. The Ottomans were Muslims, and step by step, their lands closed in around Constantinople. In 1453, they rolled out enormous cannons and fired at the walls that had stopped enemies for a thousand years. The walls finally broke, and the Byzantine Empire came to an end. Constantinople was later renamed Istanbul, and the Hagia Sophia was turned into a mosque.

That day marks the line between the Middle Ages and the modern age. Why? Because it led to two big changes. First, Byzantine scholars escaped to Italy, carrying chests of ancient Greek books, and those books helped spark the Renaissance. Second, the Ottomans and Italian merchants controlled the trade routes to the East, so spices became shockingly expensive. Europeans wanted to go around them and find their own way to Asia. That started the Age of Exploration.

Here is a quick way to tell the four empires apart. The Byzantines were Christian. The Arabs were centered in Baghdad. The Seljuks triggered the Crusades. And the Ottomans took Constantinople in 1453.

Think about this: how can the end of one city become the beginning of so many new things?

📄 中文故事稿

如果整段世界史只能記一個年份，請記住一四五三。這一年，一座撐了一千年的城市陷落了，而它的陷落，同時打開了兩扇通往新時代的門。

故事要先倒回十一世紀。那時伊斯蘭世界出現了新的強權，叫做塞爾柱帝國。塞爾柱人占領了基督徒心中的聖城耶路撒冷，也威脅到拜占庭。拜占庭向西歐求救，十一世紀末，羅馬教宗號召基督徒組成軍隊向東出發，要奪回聖城。這些士兵在衣服上縫著十字，所以叫做十字軍。

十字軍前前後後打了將近兩百年，在軍事上其實沒有多大成就。可是它帶來了一個意想不到的結果：成千上萬的歐洲人第一次親眼看見繁華的東方。他們帶回香料、絲綢和新的見聞，東西方的貿易越來越熱絡，義大利的城市也因此越來越有錢。記住，這筆錢在下一集會派上大用場。

接著登場的，是鄂圖曼帝國。鄂圖曼人信仰伊斯蘭教，勢力一步一步包圍君士坦丁堡。一四五三年，他們推出巨大的大砲，轟擊那道擋住敵人上千年的城牆。城牆終於倒下，拜占庭帝國滅亡了。君士坦丁堡後來改名伊斯坦堡，聖索菲亞大教堂也被改成了清真寺。

這一天，是中世紀和近代的分界線。為什麼？因為它帶來兩個結果。第一，拜占庭的學者帶著一箱箱古希臘的書，逃到了義大利，這些書點燃了文藝復興。第二，東西方的商路被鄂圖曼和義大利的商人牢牢控制，香料貴得嚇人，逼得歐洲人想要繞過他們，自己找路到亞洲，這就是大航海時代。

這裡有一個口訣，幫你分清四個帝國：拜基、阿巴、塞十、鄂五三。拜占庭信基督教，阿拉伯以巴格達為中心，塞爾柱引發十字軍，鄂圖曼在一四五三年滅了拜占庭。

想一想：一座城市的結束，怎麼會變成好幾件大事的開始？

第 6 集從神到人：文藝復興

這集在講什麼：文藝復興是古希臘羅馬文化的再生，三個背景是錢、書、印刷；重心從神轉向人，叫人文主義；達文西、米開朗基羅、拉斐爾是代表；但丁用家鄉語言寫《神曲》，帶動方言文學。

先認得這幾個字：rebirth（再生）、humanism（人文主義）、movable type printing（活字印刷）、the Divine Comedy（神曲）

📄 English Script（跟著聽）

Walk into a church from the Middle Ages, and the paintings on the walls show saints and angels with calm, stiff faces. The focus was religion, not people. Now walk into an artist's studio in fifteenth century Italy, and you may see a woman with a mysterious smile looking right at you, as if she is about to speak. What happened in between?

The answer is the Renaissance. From about the fourteenth to the sixteenth century, starting in Italy, Europeans rediscovered the culture of ancient Greece and Rome. The word Renaissance means rebirth.

Why did it start in Italy? Remember three things: money, books, and printing.

First, money. After the Crusades, trade between East and West boomed. Italian cities sat in the middle of the Mediterranean and made fortunes from it. Rich merchant families paid artists to create, so artists could focus on painting and sculpting.

Second, books. When the Byzantine Empire fell in 1453, scholars fled to Italy with ancient Greek books. Together with classical books that Arab scholars had translated long before, Europeans suddenly had a treasure chest of ancient wisdom.

Third, printing. Paper making traveled from China through the Arab world to Europe. Combined with movable type printing, books became cheaper. Knowledge was no longer locked inside monasteries. Ordinary people could read too.

These old books showed that the ancient Greeks cared about human beings: the human body, human ideas, and happiness in this life. Slowly, people's attention shifted from God toward people. This way of thinking is called humanism.

You can see the change in three great masters. Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa. He also studied the human body and designed flying machines. His curiosity never stopped. Michelangelo carved the statue of David and painted the moment when God reaches out to touch Adam on a chapel ceiling. Raphael painted gentle pictures of the Madonna in a meadow.

Writing changed too. Scholars used to write only in Latin. But the Italian poet Dante wrote his great poem, the Divine Comedy, in the language of his hometown, so ordinary people could understand it. Later, writers in many countries wrote in their own languages, and people felt more connected to their own nations.

Think about this: if you could rediscover one forgotten thing, what would you want to bring back?

📄 中文故事稿

走進一間中世紀的教堂，牆上的畫幾乎都是聖人和天使，表情平平的，看起來有點僵硬，因為畫的重點是宗教，不是人。可是再走進一間十五世紀義大利的畫室，你會看見一位女子帶著神祕的微笑看著你，好像下一秒就要開口說話。這中間，到底發生了什麼事？

答案是文藝復興。大約從十四到十六世紀，從義大利開始，歐洲人重新發現了古希臘、羅馬的文化。文藝復興的意思，就是再生。

為什麼偏偏是義大利？記住三個字：錢、書、印刷。

先說錢。十字軍之後，東西方貿易熱絡，義大利的城市位在地中海中央，做生意賺了大錢。富有的商人家族願意花錢請藝術家創作，藝術家才能專心畫畫、雕刻。

再說書。一四五三年拜占庭滅亡，學者帶著古希臘的書逃到義大利；加上阿拉伯人早就翻譯好的古典書籍，歐洲人一下子讀到大量古代的智慧。

最後是印刷。造紙術從中國經過阿拉伯傳到歐洲，再配上活字印刷，書變得便宜，知識不再只鎖在修道院裡，一般人也讀得到。

這些古書讓人們發現，古希臘人很重視人自己：人的身體、人的想法、人在這輩子的幸福。於是，關心的重心從神慢慢轉向人，這種想法叫做人文主義。

你可以從三位大師身上看見這種改變。達文西畫了蒙娜麗莎，他還解剖人體、設計飛行機器，好奇心多到停不下來。米開朗基羅雕出了大衛像，也在教堂天花板畫下上帝伸手觸碰亞當的那一刻。拉斐爾則畫了溫柔的草地上的聖母。口訣是：達蒙、米大創、拉草。

文學也在改變。過去讀書人都用拉丁文寫作，義大利詩人但丁卻用家鄉的語言寫下《神曲》，讓一般人也看得懂。後來各國作家紛紛用自己的語言寫作，這叫方言文學，也讓各國人民更認同自己的國家。

想一想：如果你可以重新發現一樣被遺忘的東西，你最想找回什麼？

第 7 集為了一把胡椒：大航海時代

這集在講什麼：香料經中間商轉賣太貴，歐洲人想直接航向亞洲；葡萄牙向東：狄亞士到好望角、達伽馬一四九八年到印度；西班牙向西：哥倫布一四九二年到美洲、麥哲倫船隊環球；鄭和比較早，但明朝沒有繼續遠航。

先認得這幾個字：spices（香料）、the Cape of Good Hope（好望角）、the Indies（印度一帶）、fleet（船隊）

📄 English Script（跟著聽）

Today, a small jar of pepper in your kitchen costs very little. But more than five hundred years ago in Europe, spices were as precious as jewels. People needed them to keep meat and to flavor food. The problem was that spices grew far away in Asia. On the long trip west, Ottoman and Italian traders bought and resold them again and again. By the time they reached Europe, the price had multiplied many times.

So some people began to wonder: what if we skip the old road and sail straight to Asia?

In the fifteenth century, that wild idea became possible. The compass helped ships find their way on the open sea. Shipbuilding and sailing skills improved. Kings and queens were willing to pay for voyages, and some people hoped to spread Christianity to faraway lands. And so the Age of Exploration began, lasting from about the fifteenth to the seventeenth century.

The first to set sail were Portugal and Spain, two countries on the Atlantic coast. Why not rich Italy? Because Italy was already making plenty of money on the old Mediterranean routes. The countries left out of the old road wanted a new one the most.

The two countries went in opposite directions. Portugal went east, and Spain went west.

First, Portugal. Near the end of the fifteenth century, Bartolomeu Dias sailed south along the west coast of Africa. At the southern tip, he met terrible storms. But the king gave the place a hopeful name, the Cape of Good Hope, because going around it gave hope of reaching India. In 1498, Vasco da Gama did just that. He sailed around the cape and reached India. The sea road to the East was open.

Now, Spain. In 1492, with money from the Spanish king and queen, Christopher Columbus sailed west across the Atlantic and reached land. He believed he had reached the Indies, so he called the people there Indians. In fact, he had reached the Americas, lands Europeans had never known. Later, Ferdinand Magellan's fleet kept sailing west, crossed the Pacific, and finally returned to Spain after going all the way around the world. Magellan himself died on the journey, so we say his fleet completed the voyage.

From then on, Europe's stage moved from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic.

You may remember that China's Zheng He began his great voyages in 1405, almost a hundred years before da Gama, with even bigger ships. But Ming China later stopped sailing far, while Europeans kept sailing across the whole world.

Think about this: standing in front of the same ocean, why do some people stop, while others keep going?

📄 中文故事稿

你家廚房裡的胡椒，今天一小罐沒多少錢。可是五百多年前的歐洲，香料貴得像寶石。肉要保存、食物要調味，人人都想要，可是香料長在遙遠的亞洲，一路上經過鄂圖曼和義大利商人一手一手轉賣，到了歐洲，價格已經翻了好幾倍。

於是有人開始想：如果我們不走老路，直接坐船到亞洲，會怎樣？

這個瘋狂的想法，在十五世紀變得可能。羅盤讓船在大海上也找得到方向，造船和航海技術越來越進步，再加上國王願意出錢，還有人想把基督教傳到遠方。大航海時代，就這樣開始了，大約從十五世紀一直到十七世紀。

最先出發的，是位在大西洋邊上的葡萄牙和西班牙。為什麼不是有錢的義大利？因為義大利靠地中海的老路就賺飽了，根本不需要冒險；被擋在老路外面的國家，才最想開一條新路。

兩國的方向剛好相反，記住四個字：葡東西西。葡萄牙向東，西班牙向西。

先看葡萄牙。十五世紀末，狄亞士沿著非洲西岸一路往南，在非洲最南端遇上可怕的暴風。國王卻替這個地方取了一個充滿希望的名字，好望角，因為繞過它，就有希望到達印度。一四九八年，達伽馬真的繞過好望角，抵達印度，通往東方的海路打通了。

再看西班牙。一四九二年，哥倫布得到西班牙王室的資助，一路向西橫越大西洋，到達了一片陸地。他一直以為自己到了印度，所以把當地人叫做印第安人。其實，他到的是歐洲人從來不知道的美洲。後來，麥哲倫的船隊繼續向西，橫越太平洋，最後繞地球一圈回到西班牙。麥哲倫本人死在途中，所以課本說環球航行是由船隊完成的。

從此，歐洲的舞台從地中海移到了大西洋。

你可能想起，中國的鄭和從一四零五年開始下西洋，比達伽馬早了快一百年，船隊還更大。可是明朝後來不再遠航，歐洲人卻一路航向全世界。

想一想：同樣站在大海前面，為什麼有人停下腳步，有人卻繼續往前？

第 8 集被連在一起的世界：殖民與交流

這集在講什麼：美洲古文明被西班牙消滅，天花讓原住民大量死亡，於是運入非洲黑奴；玉米、番薯和白銀改變了世界；荷蘭東印度公司一六二四年占臺灣南部；印度從蒙兀兒帝國變成英國殖民地；一七八八年英國殖民澳洲。

先認得這幾個字：smallpox（天花）、enslaved Africans（黑奴）、East India Company（東印度公司）、the Mughal Empire（蒙兀兒帝國）、colony（殖民地）

📄 English Script（跟著聽）

Once the new sea routes opened, the ocean was no longer a wall. It became a road. From this time on, the world was tied together. Some people gained a lot, and others paid a terrible price.

Let's start with the Americas. There were great civilizations here, like the Aztecs and the Incas. But the Spanish arrived with guns and horses, and quickly destroyed them. Even worse were the diseases Europeans carried, such as smallpox. The native peoples had never met these diseases and had no protection. Their population fell from tens of millions to just a few million. With so few workers left, the colonists shipped huge numbers of enslaved Africans to work in mines and on farms. The peoples of the Americas were changed forever.

But this exchange also brought things that changed the world. Corn and sweet potatoes from the Americas traveled to Europe and Asia. They could grow on hillsides and in poor soil, so they fed many more people, and the world's population grew fast. China's population boom in the Qing dynasty is one example. Large amounts of American silver also flowed into Europe and Asia and became money for trade.

Now, Asia. European countries set up East India Companies. These were unusual companies with their own armies, and they could sign treaties with local rulers. The Dutch East India Company made its headquarters in Batavia, today's Jakarta in Indonesia. In 1624, the Dutch took southern Taiwan and used it as a trading station. Two years later, the Spanish came to northern Taiwan. Right here, world history joins the history of Taiwan.

India has its own story. First came the Mughal Empire. Its founders were descendants of the Mongols, and its rulers were Muslim. The white marble Taj Mahal was built by a Mughal emperor in memory of his wife. Later, the British East India Company grew stronger step by step, and by the middle of the nineteenth century, India had become a British colony.

Finally, Australia. In 1788, Britain set up a colony there and sent prisoners to settle the land. The Aboriginal people lost their land, and many died from conflict and disease.

After eight episodes, from an Indian prince to southern Taiwan, you can see that world history is not a mess. It is one long story. Religions connected people. Empires divided the Mediterranean. The year 1453 opened two doors. And finally, the ocean tied the whole world together.

Think about this: connecting the world brought corn, and it also brought smallpox. How can we make our connections today bring more good and less harm?

📄 中文故事稿

新航路打通之後，海洋不再是牆，而變成了路。世界從這時候開始被連在一起，有人因此得到好處，也有人付出了慘痛的代價。

先看美洲。這裡原本有很發達的古文明，像是阿茲提克和印加。可是西班牙人帶著槍砲和馬匹來了，很快就把它們消滅。更可怕的，是歐洲人身上帶來的傳染病，例如天花。美洲原住民從來沒有接觸過這些病，完全沒有抵抗力，人口從幾千萬一路掉到幾百萬。少了人工作，殖民者就從非洲運來大批黑人奴隸，到礦場和農場做苦工。美洲的族群，從此徹底改變。

可是交流也帶來了改變世界的東西。美洲的玉米和番薯傳到歐洲和亞洲，它們可以種在山坡和比較貧瘠的土地上，養活了更多人，世界人口快速增加，中國清朝的人口暴增就是例子。美洲出產的大量白銀，也流進歐洲和亞洲，成為貿易的貨幣。

再看亞洲。歐洲國家成立了東印度公司，這種公司很特別，它有自己的軍隊，還可以和當地的統治者簽約。荷蘭東印度公司把總部設在今天印尼的雅加達，當時叫巴達維亞。一六二四年，荷蘭人占領臺灣南部，把臺灣當作貿易轉運站；兩年後，西班牙人也來到臺灣北部。世界史，就在這裡接上了我們熟悉的臺灣史。

印度則有另一段故事。這裡先有蒙兀兒帝國，建立者是蒙古人的後代，統治者信仰伊斯蘭教。那座白色大理石的泰姬瑪哈陵，就是蒙兀兒皇帝為了紀念妻子而蓋的。後來，英國東印度公司一步一步擴張，到了十九世紀中，印度成為英國的殖民地。

最後是澳洲。一七八八年，英國在澳洲建立殖民地，還把囚犯送去開墾，原住民的土地被奪走，許多人在衝突和疾病中死去。

八集故事走到這裡，從印度王子到臺灣南部，你會發現世界史並不雜亂，它是一條線：宗教把人連起來，帝國把地中海分開，一四五三年打開兩扇門，最後大海把整個世界綁在一起。

想一想：世界被連在一起，帶來了玉米，也帶來了天花。今天的我們，要怎麼讓連結帶來更多的好，更少的傷害？

地圖題的六個錨點

考地圖「甲乙丙丁是哪裡」時，先找到這六個點，其他位置都相對它們來找。

義大利半島地中海中間、像一隻靴子→ 羅馬、文藝復興、威尼斯
君士坦丁堡歐洲和亞洲交界的海峽→ 拜占庭首都；1453 年後被鄂圖曼占領，改稱伊斯坦堡
阿拉伯半島紅海和波斯灣之間的大半島→ 伊斯蘭教發源地
巴格達兩河流域→ 阿拉伯帝國最重要的城市
印度亞洲南方的倒三角形半島→ 佛教發源、達伽馬的終點、蒙兀兒帝國、英國殖民
好望角非洲最南端→ 葡萄牙向東航線的轉角

最容易混的五組

拜占庭帝國 vs 鄂圖曼帝國拜占庭＝東羅馬、信基督教（希臘正教）；鄂圖曼＝信伊斯蘭教，1453 年滅了拜占庭。
羅馬公教 vs 希臘正教公教＝天主教，以羅馬為中心；正教＝東正教，以君士坦丁堡為中心。
阿拉伯 vs 塞爾柱 vs 鄂圖曼依序是 8 世紀（巴格達、翻譯典籍）→ 11 世紀（引發十字軍）→ 13、14 世紀崛起（1453 滅拜占庭）。
葡萄牙 vs 西班牙航線葡萄牙向東繞非洲：狄亞士、達伽馬；西班牙向西過大西洋：哥倫布、麥哲倫。
荷蘭 vs 英國東印度公司荷蘭：總部巴達維亞（印尼），占過臺灣；英國：主要在印度。
